explanation: Return the current node if it is absent or its key matches. Otherwise recursively search the left child for a smaller key or the right child for a larger key. Return the original matching node, not a new node.
timeComplexity: O(h): only one root-to-leaf path is followed. Only one search branch is taken per level; recursive variants also retain their call frames.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursive call stack; this displayed implementation is recursive. Iteration uses only a cursor; recursion retains one frame per tree level.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/search_in_bst.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: BST ordering excludes the opposite subtree at each comparison. Induction along the selected path returns a matching node if one exists and null otherwise. No link or value changes.
walkthrough: For tree [11,5,16,2,8,13,19] and key 13, 13>11 sends the search right to 16; 13<16 sends it left to 13. Equality returns 13. The callable returns that node; the judge displays its data value. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Empty or unsuccessful search returns null/None, displayed by the wrapper as −1.
